title: California's 25th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for California's 25th Congressional District pits seven-term Democratic incumbent Raul Ruiz against Republican challenger Joe Males. The district, which has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+3, includes Imperial County and parts of Riverside and San Bernardino counties, encompassing desert communities such as Hemet, Indio, El Centro, and the Coachella Valley. Ruiz, an emergency physician and the first Latino to earn three graduate degrees from Harvard University, has held the seat since 2013 and serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee. Males, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and Hemet City Council member, is running on a platform of reducing gas taxes, rolling back regulations, and strengthening border enforcement. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Likely Democratic,' though the district swung dramatically toward Donald Trump in 2024, making it a potentially competitive general election contest.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this specific race. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Likely Democratic' as of January 15, 2026.

forecast.rationale: No public district-specific polling is available, so this forecast is based on fundamentals only. Democrat Raul Ruiz is a seven-term incumbent in a D+3 Cook PVI district, giving him a clear structural and experience advantage over Republican challenger Joe Males, a Hemet City Council member and first-time congressional candidate. Cook Political Report rates the race 'Likely Democratic.' However, the reported sharp swing toward Donald Trump in the district in 2024 suggests some erosion of Democratic support, keeping uncertainty elevated in the absence of polling. Incumbency and the Democratic lean make Ruiz a solid favorite (roughly 84% win probability), but the district is not as safe as the PVI alone might suggest.
